description: Logging in with an email address that legitimately contains an apostrophe (the same unsanitized $where-style query pt02 found by accident) crashes the login route with a full Node.js stack trace rendered as the HTTP response: internal file paths (/juice-shop/node_modules/sequelize/...), the ORM in use (Sequelize), the database engine (SQLite), and exact line numbers. The real fix for the apostrophe case itself belongs to pt02; this item measures a separate, general hygiene gap: whatever triggers an unhandled error, the response should never be a raw stack trace.
expected_exploit_indicator: An HTTP 500 response whose body contains internal file path fragments (e.g. 'node_modules/sequelize')
expected_blocked_signal: A generic error response with no file paths, library names, or stack trace content, any status code
legitimate_check: A normal, valid login must keep succeeding in every condition.
